000---Project/Brief-Paper-Summaries.title: Brief Paper Summaries
000---Project/Brief-Paper-Summaries.content:
Model-Based Optimization of Superconducting Qubit Readout
This work defined several errors by the input-output theory. Also, this work build up a model to optimize the readout errors, and apply the ex situ optimization by snake optimizer.

Error Modeling

Using input–output theory, build models for multiple readout errors, including separation error, relaxation error, and residual photon error.


Parameter Sweep

Independently vary the qubit frequency, pulse length, and pulse amplitude, and compute the corresponding error metrics for each setting.


Ex Situ Optimization

Employ a model-driven, ex situ global optimization using the Snake Optimizer to search for the parameter set that minimizes the total error.


Individualized Pulse Design

Automatically generate a unique, optimized pulse shape for each qubit, reducing the average readout error rate from ~1.9% to ~1.5% and suppressing both reset errors and leakage.





                  
                  Note 
                  
                
There is a model called “Heuristic model” which include the measurment-induced state transition

Enhancing Dispersive Readout of Superconducting Qubits through Dynamic Control of the Dispersive Shift: Experiment and Theory
This paper shows that dynamically reducing the qubit–resonator detuning Δ amplifies the dispersive shift χ, leading to higher readout SNR. A combined theoretical model (input–output theory + qubit–resonator–Purcell filter Hamiltonian) and experiment explore:

Detuning dependence

When the Purcell filter coupled with resonator, there are two eigenenergy with higher and lower frequency. Fig.2 shows dispersive shift and effective linewidth of resonator in different eigenmodes in different qubit state.


SNR and assignment error

The SNR and assignment error are defined as

\begin{aligned}
\text{SNR}&\equiv \left| \frac{\mu_{g}-\mu_{e}}{(\sigma_g+\sigma_e)/2} \right|^2 \\
\varepsilon_a &=1-F_{g, e} \\
&=[P(e|g)+P(g|e)]/2
\end{aligned}
and this article shows assignment error with different detuning and integration time which obtained the lowest error with
\Delta = -1.3 \text{ GHz}, \tau=100 \text{ ns}

Driving power

This article also demonstrate the SNR (assignment error) v.s. the photon number, which obtain the assignment error increases when n>n_{crit} which the attribute nonlinearities and measurement-induced transition.



Benchmarking the Readout of a Superconducting Qubit for Repeated Measurements

000---Project/Readout-pulse-shaping.title: Readout pulse shaping
000---Project/Readout-pulse-shaping.content:
Readout pulse shaping

In the conventional readout pulse like square pulse, it takes 10\kappa^{-1} for photon to ring down. However, by the input output theory, we can derive the input signal with given response function of photon a_T(t)^[M. Jerger et al., arXiv:2406.04891 (2024)]]:
a_{in}(t) = -\left[\frac{\kappa}{2}+i\chi_j + \frac{d}{dt} \right]a_T(t) / \sqrt{\kappa} \tag{1}
where a_T(t) is response function, usually use \sin^3(t\pi/T_p) with T_p duration.
Pulse shaping and response
  From the Eq.(1) the input signal is:

where real and imaginary part indicate the input IQ signal of the readout. This pulse shaping resulting in different responses while qubit is on different states

as you can see, this pulse shaping only works while qubit is on the ground state, hence, another equation is introduced:
a_{in}(t) = \left[\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\left(\frac{\kappa}{2}+i\chi_j+\frac{d}{dt}\right) \right]a_T(t) / \kappa^{N/2} \tag{2}
This equation shows the shape of readout pulse with transmon qubit in different states.

100---Area/Charge-dispersion.title: Charge dispersion
100---Area/Charge-dispersion.content:
Charge dispersion
In superconducting qubits, the fermionic parity leads to distinct energy levels across the Josephson junction, resulting in a frequency splitting between the two parity states—an effect known as charge dispersion. This dispersion reflects the qubit’s sensitivity to charge noise, particularly in devices with a low E_J/E_C ratio.

100---Area/Cooper-pair.title: Cooper pair
100---Area/Cooper-pair.content:
Cooper pair
Cooper pair consists of two electrons with opposite spins, and can be regarded as a boson that follows the Bose-Einstein distribution. Bosons can occupy the same quantum state. Therefore, Cooper pairs can simultaneously occupy the lowest energy state which causes the metal become to superconductor at very low temperatures.

100---Area/Idea/Vortex.title: Vortex
100---Area/Idea/Vortex.content:
Vortex
  Vortex is a small current induced by the magnetic field in superconductor. In the middle of the vortex, the superconductor exchange to normal state.
Influence
  Vortex affects the decoherence of the single junction qubit by applying the current to the junction. The fluctuations of supercurrent in the junction resulting in the pure dephasing of the qubit. Also, the vortex coupled with qubit yield a channel for qubit to loss energy.

100---Area/Parity-switch.title: Parity switch
100---Area/Parity-switch.content:
Parity switch
Parity is a property of qubit that resulting from quasiparticle(QP) tunneling. Similar to the ground state and excited state, parity also has two states: odd and even. The difference between of these states is the number of QPs in the island of Josephson junction is odd or even. The parity changes when the breaking of Cooper pairs produce QPs. In other words, the QP induced the parity changes.
The generation of QPs
The QPs resulting from the breaking of the Cooper pairs are called “resident” QPs, and it’s typically in the range 10^{-9}-10^{-5}. However, the production of QPs exceeds the expectation in unknown way. The density of QPs is out of equilibrium when the distribution is thermalized. The conjecture points out that QPs might be produced by the stray millimeter-wave photons, radioactive materials, or cosmic rays.
Source of parity switch
There are multiple possible channels for parity switch such as photon-assisted parity switch, qubit excited state induced parity switch and the QP tunneling by the thermal fluctuation^[T Connolly et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 217001 (2024)].
In superconducting qubits, the parity results in the different energy in Josephson junction which indicates the frequencies separation between two parity so called Charge dispersion.
The charge dispersion imply the sensitivity of qubit with charge noise especially in the low E_J/E_C device.

100---Area/Quasiparticle.title: Quasiparticle
100---Area/Quasiparticle.content:
Quasiparticle
The quasiparticle is a concept used to describe the phenomenon that non-exist particles traveling in a conductor or semi-conductor. In low temperature, quasiparticles usually come from the break of Cooper pair and quasiparticle usually means ==electron==.

300---Archive/Control/Drag-pulse.title: The brief introduction to DRAG pulse
300---Archive/Control/Drag-pulse.content:
Drag pulse
  The Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate (DRAG) is an analytical method designed to improve gate fidelity by reducing leakage errors^[F. Motzoi et al., Physical Review Letters 103, 110501 (2009)]. In contrast, the GRAPE pulse employs numerical optimization using the gradient descent algorithm to determine the optimal parameters that minimize leakage.
Leakage
  Qubits are typically treated as two-level systems; however, the transmon qubit used in our setup is inherently a multilevel system.  When a control pulse such as a Gaussian pulse is applied, it can unintentionally excite the third energy level, resulting in leakage, i.e., an increase in the population of the |2\rangle state. This type of leakage cannot be represented on the conventional two-dimensional Bloch sphere; instead, it manifests as a shortening of the Bloch vector, which contributes to gate errors. Moreover, the leakage dominate the total gate error.
Gaussian pulse
  Gaussian pulse suffer from the high gate error in the scale of (\epsilon^x_{max})^2/ \Delta with the short gate times. In order to quantify the gate error, the gate fidelity is define as
F_g=\frac{1}{6}\sum_{j=\pm x,\pm y, \pm z}{\mathrm{Tr}[U_{ideal}\rho_jU^\dagger_{ideal}M_P(\rho_j)]} \tag{1}
where U_{ideal} is an unitary operator of rotating frame with frequency of qubit.
Compensation to leakage error
​  When introducing the adiabatic transformation V(t)=\mathrm{exp}[-i\mathcal{E}^x(t)(\hat{\sigma}^y_{0,1}+\lambda\hat{\sigma}^y_{2,1})/2\Delta]. The transformed Hamiltonian becomes H^V=VH^RV^{\dagger}+i\hbar\dot{V}V^{\dagger} reads
\begin{aligned}
H^V/\hbar &\approx \frac{\mathcal{E}^x}{2}\hat{\sigma^x_{0,2}} 
+ \frac{\lambda\mathcal{E}^2_x}{8\Delta} 
+ \left(\delta_2+\frac{(\lambda^2+2)\mathcal{E}^2_x}{4\Delta}\right)\Pi_2 \\
&+ \left(\delta_1-\frac{(\lambda^2-4)\mathcal{E}^2_x}{4\Delta}\right)\Pi_1
+ \left[\frac{\mathcal{E}^y}{2}+\frac{\dot{\mathcal{E}^x}}{2\Delta}\right](\hat{\sigma}^y_{0,1}+\lambda\hat{\sigma}^y_{1,2}) 
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
which consists of 0-1 and 0-2 transition term, and the energy term of state |2\rangle and |1\rangle. The phase error and inertial term can be removed by giving second control with
\mathcal{E}^y=-\frac{\dot{\mathcal{E}^x}}{\Delta}\quad \mathrm{and} \quad \delta_1=\frac{(\lambda^2-4)\mathcal{E}}{4\Delta} \tag{3}
which can eliminate the leakage error to order \mathcal{E}^4_x/4\Delta
Mathematical form of pulses
  The more precision of transformation up to 5th order results in
\begin{aligned}
&\mathcal{E}^x(t)=\mathcal{E}_\pi+\frac{(\lambda^2-4)\mathcal{E}^3_\pi}{8\Delta^2}-\frac{(13\lambda^4-76\lambda^2+112)\mathcal{E}^5_\pi}{128\Delta^4}, \\
&\mathcal{E}^y(t)=-\frac{\dot{\mathcal{E}_\pi}}{\Delta}+\frac{33(\lambda^2-2)\mathcal{E}^2_\pi\dot{\mathcal{E}_\pi}}{24\Delta^3}, \\
&\delta_1(t)=\frac{(\lambda^2-4)\mathcal{E}^2_\pi}{4\Delta}-\frac{(\lambda^4-7\lambda^2+12)\mathcal{E}^4_\pi}{16\Delta^3}
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
These pluses remove most of the leakage error, for convenience of experiment, the high order term can be removed.
Weighting and detuning
  The more simple form of the DRAG pulse can be expressed as
\Omega'(t)=\Omega(t)-i\alpha \frac{\dot{\Omega}(t)}{\Delta}  \tag{5}
where \alpha is a weighting parameter, and \Delta is the anharmonicity.
  The gate fidelity of the DRAG pulse and leakage population obtained from Randomized Benchmarking (RB) imply the performance of DRAG pulse in different \alpha see Fig.1. This figure shows the DRAG pulse can not suppress phase and gate error to minimum simultaneously. However, the phase error can be minimized into the same level by change detuning^[Z. Chen et al., Physical Review Letters 116, 020501 (2016).] to against the ac-Stark shift. The detuning can be obtained by the experiment that apply \pi and -\pi multiple times:

by applying the detuning \Delta=\omega_{21}-(\omega_{10}+2\pi\delta f), the phase error can be suppressed in the same level see Fig.2. The leakage error is suppressed with \alpha=1.4.

Fig.1 This image implies the DRAG pulse enhance the gate fidelity with \alpha=0.5 and the leakage population is suppressed with \alpha=1

Fig.2 The gate fidelity and leakage rates versus DRAG weighting \alpha, measured using RB.
Comparison between DRAG and GRAPE pulse
  GRAPE pulse employs the numerical way(gradient descent) to find the best parameters to minimize the gate error. As a result, it require more time resources for training.
Compare to the DRAG pulse, the GRAPE, although, spend more time, but it is able to obtain smaller gate error.

























DRAGGRAPEApproachAnalyticalNumericalGate errorSmallSmallerMeaningPhysics derivationMathematical process
Result and gate fidelity

This fig shows error vs pulse duration with difference type of pulses: Gaussian pulse (blue solid line), Gaussian with DRAG (red dot-dashed line), tangential with DRAG (green dashed line), and GRAPE pulse (purple crosses with dotted guiding line)
  From this result, GRAPE pulse can obtain the relative small gate error with the same gate time compare to others pulses, and performance of gate fidelity is better as well.
Conclusion
  DRAG pulse can reduce the gate error by the compensation of inertial and ac-Stark shift and 0-2 transition. This also promise DRAG pulse to reach better gate error with shorter duration compare to Gaussian pulse. GRAPE reduce the gate error more then DRAG pulse, however, its’ required computing resources and time are more the DRAG pulse, and DRAG is more easy to apply to qubit.

Improvement.title: Improvement
Improvement.content:
定義主題句：

“In [system/context], a [term] refers to…”
說明這個專有名詞在該系統中的意義。



描述原因與影響：

“Such events… resulting in…”
→ 說明這個現象的物理原因與觀測到的後果。



條件強調句：

“…especially in devices with…”
→ 用來指出在哪些情況下這個問題更嚴重。



結論句/重要性句：

“…is therefore crucial for…”
→ 強調為什麼需要重視這個現象。



轉折/連接語句：

“Therefore / Thus” 因此
“Moreover / In addition / Furthermore” 更多地說
“However / whereas” 然而



文字更改
comes from → resulting from
be seems as → be regraded as
stay in → occupy
at the same time → simultaneously
called → referred to as
use → employs
need → require
so → As a result
gives → yields
another → alternative





















































可改善原用詞可更改好處動詞使用do, useapply, employ, implement, utilize更正式有力結果動詞give, getyield, achieve, obtainyield 表「產出」，achieve 表「達成指標」需要spendrequire, demand, involverequire 適用於計算資源或時間影響/好處help, fixsuppress, mitigate, enhance, reduce說明「改善」某種物理問題時用 suppress/mitigate銜接詞so, but, andtherefore, whereas, in contrast, moreover, although強化句子邏輯與說服力語序邏輯“The method is useful because it can…”“By doing X, the method can…” / “This allows…”用「by V-ing」或「which allows」強化因果邏輯名詞搭配gate error is biggate fidelity is low / leakage error is significant建議使用學術上常見的搭配詞（collocations）
